plan.contextChunk: This figure contains four tall graduated cylinders arranged side by side on a common base labeled "Oil viscosity (SAE)," each filled with motor oil of a different SAE grade — 20, 30, 40, and 50 from left to right — and each holding a metal sphere dropped simultaneously from the top so that its position at a single elapsed moment reveals the oil's resistance to flow. The oils range progressively in color from pale yellow (SAE 20) to a deeper orange-red (SAE 50), and the position of the sphere descends less and less as the SAE grade increases: the sphere has fallen to the lower portion of the tube in grade 20, slightly higher in grade 30, noticeably higher in grade 40, and only to slightly above the midpoint of the column in grade 50. Because a more viscous fluid exerts a greater drag force on the sphere, slowing it to a lower terminal velocity, the shorter distance traveled in a fixed time directly encodes the ranking of viscosity across grades. The side-by-side format at a single instant converts viscosity — an intrinsic property — into a visually comparable positional difference, removing any need for stopwatches or calculations. This figure demonstrates viscosity as a rank-orderable physical property and establishes that higher SAE-grade oils offer greater internal resistance to the motion of an object moving through them.

elements: common rectangular yellow base platform with shallow 3D thickness, trapezoidal top face, front face, and thin red outline
front base label text: Oil viscosity (SAE)
four black grade labels on the base top/front edge: 20, 30, 40, 50 from left to right
four tall transparent graduated glass cylinders arranged left to right on the common base
four pale blue-gray glass cylinder walls with subtle highlights and outlines
four open top rims with elliptical lip outlines
four small pouring-spout-like angled upper side details near the top of each cylinder
four short vertical graduation marks near the upper left inside wall of each cylinder
four gray pedestal bases under the cylinders, each with a round central foot and faceted octagonal lower plate
four oil columns of equal height inside the cylinders, ending below a clear air region at the top
SAE 20 oil fill: pale yellow column
SAE 30 oil fill: slightly deeper yellow column
SAE 40 oil fill: yellow-orange column
SAE 50 oil fill: orange-red column
four metallic gray spheres inside the oil columns, one per cylinder
sphere in SAE 20 cylinder positioned low in the oil column
sphere in SAE 30 cylinder positioned slightly higher than SAE 20
sphere in SAE 40 cylinder positioned around the middle-upper portion of the oil column
sphere in SAE 50 cylinder positioned highest among the four, slightly above the midpoint of the oil column
soft gray shadows beneath the cylinders and pedestal bases on the platform
optional terminal velocity labels next to each falling sphere
single-cylinder exploration view using one centered cylinder, one oil column whose color changes continuously from yellow to red with SAE grade, one metal sphere, and a numeric SAE label

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Separates the side-by-side ranking of the four oils from a focused view where one continuous viscosity value controls one falling ball

interactions.label: Drop spheres
interactions.teaches: Balls released together fall different distances in the same time, so the learner ranks viscosity by slower descent rather than by color or label alone

interactions.label: Oil SAE grade
interactions.teaches: As SAE grade increases, the same sphere reaches a lower terminal speed and covers less vertical distance in the same time

interactions.label: Show terminal velocity labels
interactions.teaches: Higher-viscosity oil corresponds to a smaller terminal velocity for the same sphere

demo_steps.title: Compare four oils
demo_steps.narration: The default view recreates the textbook comparison: four identical cylinders sit on one platform, labeled SAE 20, 30, 40, and 50. Starting the drop shows the balls released together, with the SAE 20 ball descending fastest and the SAE 50 ball slowest.

demo_steps.title: Reveal terminal speeds
demo_steps.narration: Turning on labels makes the rank explicit: the terminal velocity decreases from SAE 20 to SAE 50. The ball position after a fixed time is a visual proxy for how strongly each oil resists motion.

demo_steps.title: Explore one oil continuously
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the single-cylinder view and drag the SAE grade slider. The oil color deepens and the falling ball slows smoothly as the viscosity grade rises.

demo_steps.title: High-viscosity limit
demo_steps.narration: At SAE 50, the same ball descends much less during the same animation interval. The reduced distance traveled illustrates greater resistance to flow.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: common base approximately 10.8 units wide along +X, 0.45 units tall along +Y, and 2.0 units deep along +Z. Base centered at origin, with top surface around y=0 and front face visible at z=-0.9; top face is golden yellow #eacb45 with a light cream highlight, front face #e1bd3f, thin red-orange outline #c94b23. Four cylinders stand on the base at x=-3.75, -1.25, 1.25, and 3.75; all are vertical along +Y. Each glass cylinder is about 0.62 units outer diameter and 3.9 units tall, bottom of oil tube at y=0.55, top rim at y=4.45. Oil height is equal in all four cylinders: from y=0.62 to y=3.85, leaving a clear pale blue-gray air/glass region above. Glass color is very light blue-gray #c9dce3 with opacity about 0.35, outlines #8aa0a8, highlights white at low opacity. Cylinder top rims are horizontal ellipses; because the camera is slightly above, the ellipses should be visible. Each pedestal base has an octagonal plate about 1.05 units wide, 0.18 units tall, light blue-gray #d8e5e8, with a smaller circular raised foot under the tube. Grade labels sit just in front of each cylinder on the base top/front area at y=-0.08, z=-1.05: text 20, 30, 40, 50 in black, each centered under its cylinder. The main base label 'Oil viscosity (SAE)' is centered on the front vertical face, black, large. Oil colors progress left to right: SAE 20 #f3d56d pale yellow, SAE 30 #efc84e golden yellow, SAE 40 #eda65b orange-yellow, SAE 50 #f05a37 orange-red; use vertical gradient highlights so the cylinders look glossy. Metal spheres are radius about 0.23 units, dark-to-light radial material from #4b5357 to #e0e0e0 with a highlight toward upper left. Static source-like positions at the comparison snapshot: SAE 20 sphere center near y=1.25, SAE 30 near y=1.55, SAE 40 near y=2.15, SAE 50 near y=2.75, all centered in their tubes in X and slightly forward in Z so they are visible through the oil. Animation starts each sphere near y=3.55 just below the oil surface. Use relative terminal velocity model v_rel = 20 / SAE grade, giving labels approximately SAE 20: 1.00 v0, SAE 30: 0.67 v0, SAE 40: 0.50 v0, SAE 50: 0.40 v0. For a more physical descent, position may follow y(t)=y_start - K*v_rel*(t - tau*(1-exp(-t/tau))) with tau about 0.45 s and K chosen so the SAE 20 ball approaches the lower third in the source-like snapshot time. Clamp at y=0.9 so balls do not pass through the pedestal. In the single-cylinder view, use one centered cylinder at x=0 with the same dimensions; oil color interpolates from SAE 20 yellow at grade 20 to SAE 50 orange-red at grade 50, and sphere speed uses v_rel=20/grade.
interactionPlan.notes: Render glass as transparent double-sided cylinder surfaces with separate outline curves for rims and vertical edges. Render oil as a slightly smaller transparent cylinder inside each glass tube, clipped flat at the oil surface. Use billboard or CSS2D text for labels so they remain legible from the fixed camera. The dropAnimation should reset sphere centers to the common release height before each play. In four-grade comparison mode, all four balls animate simultaneously; in single SAE slider mode, only the centered cylinder and one ball are visible, and the slider updates oil color, terminal velocity label, and drop trajectory. Terminal velocity labels should appear only after the initial acceleration phase or at the side of each sphere as small callouts, e.g. 'v_t = 1.00 v0', '0.67 v0', '0.50 v0', '0.40 v0'. Keep orbit disabled by default unless the implementation provides a gentle locked orbit, because the source figure is intended as a front-facing textbook comparison.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animate all four spheres dropping simultaneously: compare falling speeds across SAE 20, 30, 40, and 50 oils to visually rank viscosity from lowest to highest
- Slider for oil SAE grade (20 to 50): watch a single ball's drop rate slow continuously as viscosity increases
- Toggle to display terminal velocity labels on each ball once each sphere reaches steady descent speed

authoredContext:
The test tubes shown here contain equal amounts of the specified motor oils. Identical metal spheres were dropped at the same time into each of the tubes, and a brief moment later, the spheres had fallen to the heights indicated in the illustration. Rank the motor oils in order of increasing viscosity, and explain your reasoning:

An image of four graduated cylinders sitting on a table labeled “Oil viscosity ( S A E )” is shown. The left-hand cylinder, labeled “20,” is mostly filled with light tan liquid and a metal ball is drawn in the lower fifth of the cylinder, but not on the bottom. The second cylinder, labeled “30,” is mostly filled with light brown liquid and a metal ball is drawn about three-fourths of the way down cylinder. The third cylinder, labeled “40,” is mostly filled with medium brown liquid and a metal ball is drawn halfway down the cylinder. The right-hand cylinder, labeled “50,” is mostly filled with brown liquid and a metal ball is drawn near the top of the liquid in the cylinder.

discrepancies: The generated figure is much more zoomed out, making the base labels and the overall apparatus appear smaller than in the source.
The numeric labels and the 'Oil viscosity (SAE)' label are far smaller and less prominent than the large textbook labels.
The cylinders are rendered with stronger 3D perspective and visible side depth, while the source is a flatter textbook illustration with nearly front-facing tubes.
The glass tops and tube outlines are somewhat more complex and transparent than the simpler pale blue caps in the source.
evaluation.notes: The main four-oil viscosity comparison is accurately represented with correct ball ordering and colors, but the default view is too small and the key base labels lack the prominence of the source.
action_items: Zoom or frame the camera closer so the platform, cylinders, and labels fill the canvas more like the source figure.
Increase the font size and visual weight of the 20, 30, 40, 50 labels and the 'Oil viscosity (SAE)' label.
Reduce the apparent perspective depth slightly to better match the flatter textbook rendering.
Simplify the top glass/cap details if aiming for closer visual fidelity to the original illustration.

feedback.rationale: The figure is conceptually accurate and highly usable with only minor visual fidelity issues around framing, label prominence, and stylistic simplification, so further iteration is not necessary.
